title: How to Make Money on Telegram: 7 Realistic Ways
seoTitle: How to Make Money on Telegram: 7 Realistic Ways (2026)
description: A practical guide to earning on Telegram: channel ad revenue, paid communities, bots, freelancing and more. What each method needs, plus the scams to avoid.
coverAlt: Kiver guide cover: How to Make Money on Telegram
body:
Telegram has roughly a billion monthly users, built-in payments, channels with no follower cap and a bot platform anyone can use for free. That makes it one of the few places where a solo creator can build a small business without paying a platform to reach their own audience. It also makes it a magnet for get-rich-quick scams. This guide covers the methods that actually exist, what each one requires, and how to spot the ones that never pay.

Key takeaways
  • Telegram shares 50% of ad revenue with channel owners, but you need a real, engaged audience first.
  • The most dependable income comes from selling something: a paid community, a bot, a service or a digital product.
  • Anything that asks you to deposit money to "unlock" earnings is a scam. Real methods never work that way.
  • Pick one method, test it with a small audience, then add a second.

7 ways to make money on Telegram

1. Earn a share of ad revenue on your channel

Telegram's official program gives channel owners 50% of the revenue from ads displayed in their channels. You can see your numbers in Channel Settings, then Statistics, then Monetization, and withdraw through Fragment. Because Telegram ads are matched to the channel rather than to personal data, your topic is your targeting. A tightly focused channel (crypto tools, language learning, local jobs) is worth more to advertisers than a general one. Eligibility rules and minimum audience sizes change, so check Telegram's current requirements before you plan around this.

2. Run a paid channel or community

Charge for access to a private channel or group: premium research, a job board, a language-learning club, a niche market newsletter, coaching with a peer group. You can collect payment with Telegram Stars subscriptions or an external payment provider connected through a bot. The rule that decides whether this works is recurring value. People pay monthly for something new every week, not for an archive. A common pattern is a free public channel that proves your quality and a paid tier for the deeper material. If your niche touches financial advice or investment signals, check the regulations in your country first.

3. Build a bot or mini app people pay for

Bots are software that lives inside Telegram, and software can charge. Common models are a free tier plus a paid plan, pay-per-use credits, or one-time purchases. Digital goods sold inside bots and mini apps are generally expected to use Telegram Stars, so read the current Bot Payments documentation before you design your pricing. A bot needs far less audience than a channel because discovery happens through directories and search. If you have never built one, start with our guide on how to create a Telegram bot.

4. Sell your skills as a freelancer

Businesses and creators keep asking for the same things: custom bots, mini apps, channel setup, community moderation, copywriting and growth. You can find clients in Telegram job channels, freelance marketplaces and by direct outreach. Your best portfolio is your own work, so build two or three small bots and list them on Kiver where a client can see them live.

5. Use affiliate links and referral programs

Recommend tools you actually use, such as hosting, design tools or apps, and earn a commission when someone signs up. It works best inside a channel that already has trust. Always disclose affiliate links, keep them relevant to the post, and avoid dropping links in other people's groups: most communities ban that quickly.

6. Sell sponsored posts directly

Once your channel has a consistent niche audience, brands in that niche will pay to be featured. Price by average views per post and audience quality, not just subscriber count, and keep sponsored content clearly labelled and sparse so the channel stays worth reading.

7. Sell digital products

Templates, guides, presets, spreadsheets, short courses and tools are cheap to produce once and can be delivered automatically by a bot after payment. Your channel is the shop window, the bot is the checkout and delivery.

Which method fits you?

The table below rates each method by how big an audience you need, how much ongoing work it takes and what kind of income it produces. If you are starting from zero, the methods with a low audience requirement (bots, freelancing) are usually the fastest way to a first payment.

A simple roadmap from zero to first income

  1. Pick one niche. One topic and one audience beats a general channel every time.
  2. Give value for free. Start a channel, a bot or a stream of useful posts so people have a reason to follow you.
  3. Find your first 100 people. Use relevant communities, directories like the Kiver directory, and trackable deep links.
  4. Add one offer. Ads, a paid tier or a product. One, not five.
  5. Measure and repeat. Keep what converts, drop what does not.

Scams to avoid

Because Telegram is open and fast, it is full of fake money-making schemes. Walk away from any of these:

  • Anything that asks you to deposit money before you can "unlock" or "withdraw" earnings.
  • Guaranteed daily returns, "risk-free" trading signals or bots that promise profit.
  • "Task" or "like and subscribe" jobs that pay a little, then demand a fee to pay out more.
  • Referral pyramids where income depends on recruiting others.
  • Strangers who message you a job offer, or any bot that asks for your seed phrase or login code.

If something looks like this, use Telegram's Report option and move on. A real method makes you money by serving customers or an audience, not by taking your deposit.

Your next step

The lowest-risk path for most people is to build one small, useful bot and put it where users can find it. Launch your bot on Kiver and it gets a permanent, indexable page in a directory people already browse, or explore what others have built in the bot directory for ideas.

faq.q: How much money can you make on Telegram?
faq.a: There is no honest single number. Ad revenue scales with channel views, paid communities with price multiplied by members and retention, and freelancing with your rates and client load. Anyone quoting a typical income without showing the math is usually selling something.

faq.q: Do I need a big audience to make money on Telegram?
faq.a: Not for every method. Building bots, freelancing and selling digital products can work with a small audience. Ad revenue sharing and sponsored posts need a larger, engaged one.

faq.q: Can you make money with a Telegram bot?
faq.a: Yes. Common models are subscriptions, pay-per-use credits and premium tiers, plus building bots for clients as a freelancer. Digital goods sold in bots generally use Telegram Stars.
Creating a channel or a bot costs nothing. Hosting a bot ranges from free tiers to a few dollars a month, depending on traffic.

faq.q: Do I have to pay tax on Telegram income?
faq.a: In most countries, yes. Rules vary by location, so this is not tax advice. Check with a local accountant or your tax authority.

title: How to Create a Telegram Bot in 30 Minutes
seoTitle: How to Create a Telegram Bot: Step-by-Step Guide (2026)
description: Create a Telegram bot with BotFather, write working code in Python or Node.js, host it and secure your token. A beginner-friendly step-by-step tutorial.
coverAlt: Kiver tutorial cover: How to Create a Telegram Bot
body:
A Telegram bot is a small program that talks to people through the Telegram app, and creating one is free and takes about half an hour. You do not need a company, an API key from anyone but Telegram, or even a server to get started. This guide walks from zero to a working bot and then to the part most tutorials skip: hosting it, keeping it secure and getting people to find it.

Key takeaways
  • Every bot starts in a chat with @BotFather, which gives you a secret token.
  • Your code receives messages from Telegram (long polling or webhook) and replies through the Bot API.
  • Never publish your token. If it leaks, revoke it in BotFather straight away.
  • Once it works, list it in a directory so real users can discover it.

How a Telegram bot works

When someone messages your bot, Telegram turns that message into an update. Your server gets the update, decides what to do, and sends a reply through the Bot API. That is the whole model. The only choice you make is how updates reach your code: long polling (your code repeatedly asks Telegram for new updates, simplest while developing) or a webhook (Telegram sends updates to an HTTPS URL on your server, better for production and serverless hosting).

Step 1: Create the bot with BotFather

  1. Open Telegram and search for @BotFather, the official bot for creating bots. Check for the verified badge.
  2. Send /newbot.
  3. Choose a display name, for example "Daily Quotes".
  4. Choose a username. It must be unique and end in bot, for example dailyquotes_bot.
  5. BotFather replies with an API token. Copy it somewhere safe. Anyone with this token controls your bot.

Step 2: Choose how to build it

You have two realistic paths:

  • No-code builders let you drag together menus and replies. They are fast for simple FAQ, lead-capture or menu bots but limit custom logic.
  • Code gives full control. Popular libraries are python-telegram-bot and aiogram for Python, and grammY and Telegraf for Node.js. If you can write a basic script, start here.

Here is a complete "hello world" bot in Node.js with grammY:

import { Bot } from "grammy";

const bot = new Bot(process.env.BOT_TOKEN);

bot.command("start", (ctx) => ctx.reply("Hi! I'm alive."));
bot.on("message:text", (ctx) => ctx.reply("You said: " + ctx.message.text));

bot.start();

And the same idea in Python with python-telegram-bot:

import os
from telegram import Update
from telegram.ext import ApplicationBuilder, CommandHandler, ContextTypes

async def start(update: Update, context: ContextTypes.DEFAULT_TYPE):
    await update.message.reply_text("Hi! I'm alive.")

app = ApplicationBuilder().token(os.environ["BOT_TOKEN"]).build()
app.add_handler(CommandHandler("start", start))
app.run_polling()

Store your token in an environment variable, as shown, instead of writing it into the file.

Step 3: Run it and test

Start the script, open your bot in Telegram, press Start and send a message. If it replies, you have a working bot. While you develop, long polling is fine because it runs from your laptop with no public URL needed.

Step 4: Host it so it stays online

A bot only answers while its code is running. Your main options:

  • A small always-on service on a platform like Render or Railway, or a cheap VPS, running long polling or a webhook.
  • Serverless functions (for example on Vercel) with a webhook. You register the URL once with setWebhook and Telegram calls it for every update. Cold starts mean slower first replies, so keep handlers fast.

Webhooks must use HTTPS. Whichever host you choose, set the bot token as a secret environment variable there too.

Step 5: Polish the bot's profile

This is where users decide whether to press Start, so spend ten minutes on it. In BotFather use /setdescription for the text people see before they start, /setuserpic for a clear profile photo, and /setcommands to create the command menu. Write the description as a one-line promise: what the bot does and for whom.

Security basics

  • Never commit the token to GitHub. Public repositories are scanned for leaked tokens constantly.
  • If the token leaks, send /revoke to BotFather and update your hosting secret.
  • Validate and limit user input, especially if the bot calls paid APIs, so one user cannot run up your bill.
  • Be honest about data. Say what you store and why, and follow Telegram's Bot Platform terms.

Step 6: Get your first users

A working bot nobody can find earns nothing. Submit it to a directory so it has a permanent public page, then share it where your audience already is. On Kiver, you paste your t.me link, pick a category and your bot gets a listing people can search, upvote and share. Launch your bot on Kiver, then read how to get your first 100 users and how bots can earn money.

faq.q: Is it free to create a Telegram bot?
faq.a: Yes. Creating a bot with BotFather is free. You only pay if you choose a paid hosting plan or use paid third-party APIs.

faq.q: Do I need to know how to code to make a Telegram bot?
faq.a: No. No-code builders cover simple menu and FAQ bots. For custom logic, payments or integrations, basic coding in Python or JavaScript helps a lot.

faq.q: What is the difference between polling and webhooks?
faq.a: With long polling your code keeps asking Telegram for new updates. With a webhook Telegram sends each update to your HTTPS URL. Polling is easier for development; webhooks suit production and serverless hosting.

faq.q: Why must a bot username end in 'bot'?
faq.a: It is a Telegram rule that makes bots easy to recognise. Pick a short, memorable name that describes what the bot does.

faq.q: How do I get people to use my bot?
faq.a: List it in a directory such as Kiver, share it in relevant communities, give it a clear description and a great first message, and use deep links to see which channels bring users.

title: How to Promote a Telegram Bot: 9 Ways to Get Your First 100 Users
seoTitle: How to Promote a Telegram Bot: 9 Ways to Get Users (2026)
description: Nine practical ways to get your first 100 users for a Telegram bot, from directory listings and deep links to community help, content and retention.
coverAlt: Kiver growth cover: How to Promote a Telegram Bot
body:
Most Telegram bots fail for a boring reason: nobody finds them. Building the bot is the easy part. This guide covers nine practical ways to get your first 100 users, how to tell which ones work, and the mistakes that get bots banned from groups.

Key takeaways
  • Fix the first 60 seconds of the experience before you promote anything.
  • Use deep links so you know which channel each user came from.
  • Be useful in communities instead of posting links. Spam gets you removed.
  • Track return visits, not just sign-ups: retention tells you if the bot is worth promoting.

Think in a funnel

Every bot loses people at each step between discovering it and sharing it. Promotion only pays off if the steps after discovery work, so know where your drop-off is before you spend effort on traffic.

9 ways to get your first 100 users

1. Nail the first 60 seconds

Before promoting, press Start on your own bot as a stranger would. Does the welcome message say what the bot does and what to tap next? Can a new user get a result within a minute? A confusing first screen wastes every visitor you work to bring in.

2. Write a clear name and description

Your name and the description shown before Start are your landing page. Lead with the outcome ("Convert voice notes to text") rather than the technology ("AI-powered multi-modal assistant").

3. List it in a bot directory

People actively browse and search directories for bots, and a listing gives you a permanent, indexable page that search engines can find. Submit your bot to Kiver: paste your t.me link, choose a category and your bot gets a public page with votes and a shareable URL.

4. Use deep links to track sources

A link like t.me/yourbot?start=reddit passes a start parameter to your bot. Give every channel its own parameter (letters, numbers, underscores and hyphens, up to 64 characters) and log it, so you can see which source brings users who actually stay.

5. Be helpful in communities

Find groups and forums where people ask for what your bot does. Answer questions properly first, mention the bot only where it is genuinely the answer, and read each group's rules. Dropping links is the fastest way to get banned.

6. Build a channel for updates

A small public channel gives you somewhere to announce features, share tips and collect feedback, and it lets users follow you without having to open the bot.

7. Add sharing to the product

Let users share a result, a referral link or a "send to a friend" button. If your bot supports inline mode, using it in any chat shows the bot to everyone in that conversation.

8. Publish useful content

Write the guide your target user is searching for: a tutorial, a comparison, a template. Content brings steady, free traffic over time and builds trust before anyone opens the bot.

9. Try paid ads only after retention is healthy

Telegram has its own ad platform, but paying to send people into a leaky funnel just wastes money. Run ads once users come back and your cost per returning user makes sense.

What to measure

  • Start rate: of people who open the chat, how many press Start?
  • Activation: how many get a first useful result?
  • Return rate: how many come back the next day and the next week?
  • Source quality: which deep-link source produces users who return?

Mistakes that hurt growth

  • Spamming links in groups, which gets the bot and you reported.
  • Buying fake users. They never return and make your numbers useless.
  • Sending too many broadcast messages, which makes users block the bot.
  • Promoting before the bot is reliable. Downtime on launch day is hard to recover from.

Next steps

Put your bot where people browse for bots. Launch it on Kiver, then look at how other makers present theirs in the bot directory. New to building? Start with how to create a Telegram bot, and if you want to earn from it, read how to make money on Telegram.

faq.q: How do I get my first users for a Telegram bot?
faq.a: Polish the first-run experience, list the bot in a directory like Kiver, answer questions in relevant communities, and share deep links so you can see which source works.

faq.q: What is a Telegram deep link?
faq.a: A link in the form t.me/yourbot?start=parameter. When someone opens it and presses Start, your bot receives the parameter, which you can use to track the source of each user.

faq.q: Can I buy users for my Telegram bot?
faq.a: You can, but purchased users rarely return or pay, and they distort your metrics. Real, relevant users from communities and directories are worth far more.

faq.q: How long does it take to get 100 users?
faq.a: It depends on your niche and effort. Bots that solve a specific problem and are listed where people search tend to reach their first 100 users much faster than general-purpose bots.

faq.q: Should I use Telegram Ads to promote my bot?
faq.a: Only after your bot retains users. Ads send traffic fast, but if the first-run experience is weak you pay for visitors who leave.
